items.title: Griekspoor pega un tremendo palo a Zverev: "Me cuesta verle jugar"
items.description: Contundentes palabras del neerlandés, que señala que no vio la final del pasado US Open y se unió a las críticas de compañeros de vestuario por la excesiva cantidad de botes que necesita el germano.

items.title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
items.description: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.

items.title: Ferrer va a por Chile con Jódar y Mérida en los individuales
items.description: El sorteo de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis entre España y Chile por un puesto en la Finales hace que abran el fuego Tabilo y Mérida, seguido del Garín - Jódar. Martínez y Munar serán la apuesta del dobles.

items.title: El Top 100 ya no tiene adolescentes
items.description: Jódar era el único en el top 100 del ranking ATP, pero tras cumplir 20 años deja de ser adolescente y la clasificación mundial, por primera vez en una década se queda sin ‘niños’.

items.title: "Alcaraz estuvo muy cerca de su mejor nivel en el US Open"
items.description: Renzo Furlan, entrenador italiano, destacó el gran hacer del Alcaraz en el US Open, mientras que apuntó que Zverev puede luchar por el número uno ante Sinner.

items.title: La ATP y la WTA estudian una huida de Oriente Medio
items.description: Los conflictos bélicos y la situación vivida en 2026 han provocado que ambas organizaciones barajen sustituir los torneos de Doha y Dubái por el bien de los tenistas.

items.title: La dura crítica de Mouratoglou a la actitud de Sabalenka
items.description: El reputado entrenador francés cree que la tenista bielorrusa se está dejando llevar demasiado por sus emociones, lo que afecta a su nivel.

items.title: El terrible testimonio de J.J. Wolf sobre su lesión de hombro
items.description: El tenista estadounidense ha relatado el terrible incidente que le mantuvo un año alejado del circuito y que le afectó de lleno incluso a su vida cotidiana.

items.title: Fritz señala el gran problema del tenis: “Las pelotas son cada vez más lentas”
items.description: El estadounidense no se muerden la lengua y estalla indignado ante el tipo de bola con el que se juega actualmente en el circuito profesional: "Es muy desmotivado, no puedo entrenar en las mismas condiciones que compito".

items.title: El final más inesperado para Ram y Salisbury
items.description: Quizá pasó algo desapercibido, pero Rajeev Ram anunció su retirada del tenis tras su último partido en el US Open 2026. Lo que nadie esperaba es que su compañero de batalla, Joe Salisbury, anunciara ayer el mismo destino.

items.title: Kostyuk into Guadalajara last eight without playing a point
items.description: Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament.

items.title: Rafa Jódar cumple 20 años: ¿qué habían hecho otras leyendas a su edad?
items.description: Hoy, jueves 17 de septiembre, Rafa Jódar cumple 20 años. Y lo hace a las puertas de su debut en Copa Davis, a un paso del top10 y firmando la mayor progresión de la temporada dentro de la ATP. ¿Se le puede comparar con las leyendas más recientes?

items.title: Investigating the exploitation of girls by drug gangs
items.description: A look at two decades of failure to protect girls exploited and raped by drug gangs.

items.title: Charlotte to host WTA Finals from 2027
items.description: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.

items.title: More than the Score
items.description: It's been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title

items.title: Draper decides not to play again this season
items.description: Former world number four Jack Draper will not play again this season, but says he is aiming to return to the tour at the start of next year.

items.title: From Challenger Tour to Davis Cup - GB's Samuel on 'surreal' year
items.description: Briton Toby Samuel is to make his Davis Cup debut for Great Britain after what he calls a "surreal" 12 months.

items.title: Zverev wins US Open to earn second Grand Slam victory
items.description: Alexander Zverev wins the second Grand Slam of his career by beating Ben Shelton 6-3, 6-6 (7-6), 5-7, 6-2 in the final of the US Open.

items.title: 'It feels amazing' - Zverev reflects on US Open win
items.description: Alexander Zverev says it was an "amazing feeling" to lift the US Open trophy after defeating Ben Shelton in the final.

items.title: Episode 2: There's always a contender
items.description: There’s a new number one - but not everything is easy when you’re at the top.

items.title: Zverev turns US Open tears into triumph
items.description: How a more composed Alexander Zverev stayed 'zen-like' to beat Ben Shelton and win the US Open, six years after a heart-breaking defeat in the final.

items.title: Zverev caps transformational year with US Open triumph
items.description: Alexander Zverev lands his second Grand Slam title after ending Ben Shelton's hopes of becoming a rare home US Open men's champion.

items.title: Rybakina beats Sabalenka to win US Open for the first time
items.description: Elena Rybakina beats the two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open and her third Grand Slam title overall.

items.title: 'Tough to control emotions' as Sabalenka suffers another near miss
items.description: After losing another Grand Slam final, Aryna Sabalenka smashes her racquet in frustration at a year that has seen her lose her world number one status.

items.title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed
items.description: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.

items.title: Rybakina wins US Open to inflict further pain on Sabalenka
items.description: Elena Rybakina demonstrates why she is the best women's player in the world by beating Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.

items.title: Only Roland Garros towel left - Yastremska says flat destroyed by missile
items.description: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.

items.title: GB's Hewett beats Oda to win fifth US Open title
items.description: Great Britain's Alfie Hewett beats Japanese top seed Tokito Oda to win a fifth US Open title and his 11th Grand Slam singles crown overall.

items.title: 'I'm still in shock' - GB's Skupski wins US Open doubles title with Harrison
items.description: Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison win the US Open men's doubles to secure their second Grand Slam title together.

items.title: American Shelton to face Zverev in US Open final
items.description: Ben Shelton powers past Frances Tiafoe in an all-American US Open semi-final to earn a spot in Sunday's final against number one seed Alexander Zverev.

items.title: US Open pays tribute on 25th anniversary of 9/11
items.description: The US Open pauses to remember the victims of the 9/11 attacks that took place 25 years ago.

items.title: Hewett and Reid secure sixth US Open doubles title
items.description: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid come from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time at the US Open.

items.title: Townsend & Siniakova complete career Slam in New York
items.description: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend win the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam.

items.title: Bed at 6:45am - US Open semi-finalists fight effects of late-night finishes
items.description: New York is known as the city that never sleeps. But that comes at a price for US Open stars - including men's semi-finalists Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev.

items.title: GB's Salisbury & Ram beat champions to reach semis
items.description: Three-time US Open doubles champions Joe Salisbury and Rajeev Ram beat last year's winners Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos to reach the semi-finals.

items.title: Gauff saves match points to set up Rybakina semi-final
items.description: Coco Gauff saves two match points to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina.

items.title: 'Just a number' - Rybakina's rise to world number one
items.description: Elena Rybakina becomes the new women's world number one after reaching the US Open semi-finals, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top of the rankings.

items.title: Shelton reaches semis after beating Alcaraz in five-set epic
items.description: Watch highlights from Ben Shelton's thrilling five-set win over Carlos Alcaraz at the US Open which finished at 03:34 local time.

items.title: Shelton beats Alcaraz in latest-ever US Open finish to reach semis
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence is over after a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ends at 03:34 local time.

items.title: Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits
items.description: Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".

items.title: More than the Score
items.description: Crowd behaviour has been in the spotlight at the US Open

items.title: Williams sisters crash out of US Open after losing to Chan and Joint
items.description: Venus and Serena Williams fell short against 14th seeds Chan Hao-Ching and Maya Joint who beat them 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) in front of a roaring Arthur Ashe stadium at the US Open.

items.title: No Brits left in US Open singles - but are there reasons to be positive?
items.description: There will be no British interest in the second week of another Grand Slam at the US Open - but is it all doom and gloom?

items.title: Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold?
items.description: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New York.

items.title: Watch: Djokovic overcome with emotion during US Open loss
items.description: Novak Djokovic breaks down in tears during his first-round loss in the US Open against Argentina's Mariano Navone.

items.title: Williams and Alcaraz team up at US Open
items.description: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz take on Flavio Coboilli and Belinda Bencic in the mixed doubles at the US Open, eventually losing 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.

items.title: 'I feel I am imprisoning myself' - Djokovic on doubts, childhood and future
items.description: Novak Djokovic discusses being his own biggest doubter and the Belgrade childhood that shaped him in a new documentary.

items.title: Why positive cocaine test could mean end of Kyrgios' career
items.description: Nick Kyrgios once said he did not want to play tennis into his 30s. A positive cocaine test could have brought an end to his career aged 31.

items.title: Dog walk and expletive text - key findings in Vondrousova anti-doping case
items.description: The full report into 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova's four-year ban for refusing a doping test has been released - BBC Sport analyses the key findings.

items.title: 'Out of this world!' - Best shots of Wimbledon 2026
items.description: Enjoy the best shots of Wimbledon 2026, featuring Great Britain's Arthur Fery, Novak Djokovic, Coco Gauff and more.

items.title: From shock loss to Wimbledon title - resilient Sinner rises back to top
items.description: For a brief moment after his shock French Open loss, Jannik Sinner appeared vulnerable. He answered the critics by storming to a second Wimbledon title.

items.title: Sinner beats Zverev in thriller to retain Wimbledon title
items.description: Jannik Sinner comes from a set down to defeat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7-9) 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 6-4 to retain his Wimbledon title.

items.title: How Sinner slid his way to Wimbledon glory
items.description: BBC Sport's Jamie Murray, Tim Henman and Todd Woodbridge analyse Jannik Sinner's Wimbledon final victory against Alexander Zverev.

items.title: Wimbledon crowd 'played big part' in me reaching final - Zverev
items.description: After his defeat to Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev reflected on how the Wimbledon crowd "played a big part" in his journey to the final.

items.title: 'It takes two' - Sinner praises Zverev for pushing him in 'amazing' final
items.description: Jannik Sinner says Alexander Zverev can be a Wimbledon champion soon and promises to "be very, very careful" as the German challenges his world number one status, following a four-set win for Sinner in the final of the grass-court Grand Slam.

items.title: Sinner's best shots as world number one retains Wimbledon title
items.description: Enjoy the best of Jannik Sinner's title-retaining performance, as the world number one defeats Alexander Zverev in four sets in the men's singles final at Wimbledon 2026.

items.title: 'Sweet Sinner' wraps up 'compelling' final to retain title
items.description: Jannik Sinner brings Centre Court to its feet, winning a brilliant rally before wrapping up a "compelling" Wimbledon final against Alexander Zverev to retain the men's singles title.

items.title: Why Wimbledon is more special to Sinner than other majors
items.description: Jannik Sinner says tennis was only his third sport growing up, behind skiing and football, except during Wimbledon, the one major he watched and the tournament that sparked his love of grass.

items.title: Why is Zverev allowed to use a phone during his matches?
items.description: Alexander Zverev explains how he uses a mobile phone to monitor his blood glucose levels when he is playing, as the Wimbledon finalist suffers from Type 1 Diabetes.

items.title: Oda beats GB's Hewett to retain Wimbledon wheelchair title
items.description: Japan's Tokito Oda defeats Great Britain's Alfie Hewett in straight sets to retain his Wimbledon wheelchair men's singles title.
